context.title: The Foundling Bride
context.summary: In a long, graphic allegory, Jerusalem is an abandoned baby girl whom God rescues, raises and marries, but who betrays him; yet he promises to remember his covenant and make atonement.
context.background: The story shocks deliberately to expose spiritual unfaithfulness. Jerusalem's origin is called Canaanite (v. 3), puncturing national pride. Her 'sisters' Samaria and Sodom were bywords for judgment, yet Jerusalem has outdone them (vv. 46–52); Sodom's sin is named as pride, plenty and neglect of the poor (v. 49).

customs.note: A newborn's cord was cut, the baby washed, rubbed with salt and wrapped snugly in cloth. This child received none of it and was left to die.
Covering someone with the corner of one's garment was a gesture of protection and marriage, as in Ruth 3:9.

watchFor: God's 'Live' spoken over the dying baby (v. 6).
The surprising ending: an everlasting covenant (vv. 60–63).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Chaldea
places.summary: The southern portion of Babylonia, Lower Mesopotamia, lying chiefly on the right bank of the Euphrates, but commonly used of the whole of the Mesopotamian plain.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

events.title: Prophecies of Ezekiel
events.summary: Passage: Ezekiel 1:1–48:35. People: Ezekiel. Lasted about 23 years.
